transliteration_key.g: ج (في مصر تُنطق g مثل gate)

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Good morning, Karim.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، بس لسه نعسانة شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdu lillah, bas lessa na3saana shwayya.
dialogue.english: Praise God, but I'm still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: It's a quarter past seven.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: يا نهار أبيض! لازم أنزل بسرعة، عندي شغل الساعة تمانية.
dialogue.transliteration: ya nahaar abyad! laazem anzel bsor3a, 3andi shoghl es-saa3a tamaanya.
dialogue.english: Oh no! I have to leave quickly, I have work at eight.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: مش هتشرب قهوة قبل ما تنزل؟
dialogue.english: Aren't you going to drink coffee before you leave?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Yes, but quickly, there's no time.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Here, drink and head off to work.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll see you in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: مع السلامة، خلي بالك من نفسك.
dialogue.transliteration: ma3a s-salaama, khalli baalak men nafsak.
dialogue.english: Bye, take care of yourself.

response.english: Yes, I woke up at six.

pair.english: Do you want coffee first thing?

response.arabic: أكيد، مقدرش أعيش من غير قهوة
response.english: Of course, I can't live without coffee.

lessons.culture: Egyptians answer صباح الخير with صباح النور, and friends often play with it: صباح الفل, صباح الورد. A quick tea or coffee before leaving the house is close to universal, even on a rushed morning.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but literary; it is not the everyday reply to a morning greeting.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to صباح الخير is صباح النور; صباح الفل and صباح الورد are the friendly variants.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "الساعة كام دلوقتي؟" Answer that it's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: This is a bookish way to say the time; nobody says it like this out loud.

exercises.tip: الساعة + number is the everyday pattern for telling the time.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "عايز _____ أول حاجة." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: This wording is more explicit and formal than the simple everyday word.

exercises.tip: أول حاجة means first thing, before anything else.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الدنيا _____ أوي الصبح بدري." English meaning: Early morning is very cold.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but reads like a written weather report, not spoken Egyptian.

exercises.tip: الدنيا برد and الدنيا ساقعة are both how Egyptians say it is cold out.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Egyptian speech.

exercises.tip: صحيت is the everyday Egyptian verb for woke up; بدري means early.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: This is grammatical but far too formal for everyday complaining about a bus.

exercises.tip: فاتني is used for missing a bus, a train, or any chance that passed.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm still sleepy."

too_formal.feedback: This is textbook Arabic; لسه is the natural spoken word for still.

exercises.tip: لسه before an adjective is how still is said; a woman says نعسانة.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I left for work"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is written-style Arabic, not the spoken phrase being practised.

exercises.tip: نزلت على الشغل literally means I went down to work; Egyptians say نزلت for leaving the house.

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "صباح الخير" best?

too_formal.feedback: Just repeating صباح الخير back sounds stiff; a real reply changes the word.

exercises.tip: صباح النور, صباح الفل and صباح الورد are all natural replies to a morning greeting.

exercises.prompt: Put these pieces in a natural order: "بدري / على الشغل / نزلت"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this word order and vocabulary belong to written Arabic.

exercises.tip: Verb, then place, then time is the natural spoken order, though the time can also come before the place.

reply.arabic: بِاتْغَدَى في الْمَطْعَم اللي جَنْب الشُّغِل
reply.english: I have lunch at the restaurant next to work.

phrases.arabic: لازِم أخْلِص الْحَاجَة دِي قَبْل الضُّهْر

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Did you get to work, Karim?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، وصلت من ساعة، عندي اجتماع الساعة عشرة.
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, wesilt men saa3a, 3andi egtimaa3 es-saa3a 3ashra.
dialogue.english: Yes, I got here an hour ago, I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Okay, do you have a lot of work today?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، عندي شغل كتير دلوقتي، ولازم أخلص الحاجة دي قبل الضهر.
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, 3andi shoghl ketir dilwa2ti, w laazem akhallas el-7aaga di 2abl ed-dohr.
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a lot of work now, and I have to finish this before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: أنا تعبانة شوية دلوقتي، وبدور على القلم بتاعي.
dialogue.transliteration: ana ta3baana shwayya dilwa2ti, w badawwar 3ala el-2alam bitaa3i.
dialogue.english: I'm a bit tired now, and I'm looking for my pen.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: I saw it on the desk a moment ago.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Thanks! Where are you having lunch today?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: في المطعم اللي جنب الشغل. تيجي معايا؟
dialogue.transliteration: fil-maT3am elli ganb esh-shoghl. teegi ma3aaya?
dialogue.english: At the restaurant next to work. Will you come with me?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: يلا، أنا جعانة وعايزة آكل حاجة.
dialogue.english: Sure, I'm hungry and I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: هكلمك بعد الضهر لما أخلص الاجتماع.
dialogue.transliteration: hakallemek ba3d ed-dohr lamma akhallas el-egtimaa3.
dialogue.english: I'll call you in the afternoon when I finish the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Great, good luck with it.

response.english: Yes, I arrived an hour ago.

response.arabic: بِاتْغَدَى في الْمَطْعَم اللي جَنْب الشُّغِل
response.english: I have lunch at the restaurant next to work.

lessons.culture: In Egypt lunch (الغدا) is the main meal of the day and is often eaten in the mid-afternoon rather than at noon, so بعد الضهر covers a long stretch. Asking for a short break with ينفع is polite, and خد راحتك is the warm, standard answer.

exercises.prompt: A colleague asks you: "بتتغدى فين؟" Say you have lunch at the restaurant next to work.
exercises.answer: بِاتْغَدَى في الْمَطْعَم اللي جَنْب الشُّغِل
accepted: بِاتْغَدَى في الْمَطْعَم اللي جَنْب الشُّغِل

too_formal.item: أتناول الغداء في المطعم المجاور للعمل
too_formal.feedback: This is correct but written-style; it is not how a colleague would answer out loud.

exercises.tip: اللي means which or that, and جنب means next to.

exercises.prompt: You ask your boss "ينفع آخد استراحة؟" and he says yes warmly. What does he say?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but stiff; it is not the friendly everyday answer.

exercises.tip: خد راحتك literally means take your comfort, and it is said for take your time or go ahead.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "عندي _____ الساعة عشرة." English meaning: I have a meeting at ten.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but more formal than the everyday word for a meeting.

exercises.tip: Egyptians say اجتماع, and ميتينج is just as common in offices.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "أنا جعان، _____ آكل حاجة." English meaning: I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, but not how it is said in Egyptian speech.

exercises.tip: عايز (or عاوز) is the everyday Egyptian I want; a woman says عايزة.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "I arrived at work."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but written-style; Egyptians drop the preposition in speech.

exercises.tip: وصلت takes its place directly: وصلت الشغل, وصلت البيت.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I have to finish this task before noon."
exercises.answer: لازِم أخْلِص الْحَاجَة دِي قَبْل الضُّهْر
accepted: لازِم أخْلِص الْحَاجَة دِي قَبْل الضُّهْر
لازم أخلص الشغل ده قبل الضهر
لازم أخلص الحاجة دي قبل الظهر

too_formal.item: يجب أن أنهي هذه المهمة قبل الظهر
too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, but nobody says it like this at work.

exercises.tip: لازم plus a verb is the everyday way to say I have to; الحاجة دي is this thing.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm looking for my pen."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not the spoken form.

exercises.tip: بدور على means I'm looking for; بتاعي is the Egyptian word for mine.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I finished my work early today"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is written Arabic, not what is being practised.

exercises.tip: النهارده means today; خلصت is the everyday verb for I finished.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "What's the news today?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is how a news anchor would say it, not a friend.

exercises.tip: إيه is the Egyptian word for what, and الأخبار is used as a friendly how are things.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "دلوقتي / كتير / شغل / عندي"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is written Arabic, not the spoken sentence.

exercises.tip: عندي + thing is how Egyptians say I have; دلوقتي can come first or last.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Good evening, Mona.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Good evening, you're back home at last?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Yes, I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Do you want to shower first?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, w ba3d keda hanet3ashsha eh?
dialogue.english: Yes, and after that what will we eat for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: هعمل أكل خفيف، وبعدين تحب نتفرج على مسلسل؟
dialogue.transliteration: ha3mel akl khafeef, w ba3deen te7ebb netfarrag 3ala mosalsal?
dialogue.english: I'll make something light, and then do you want to watch a series?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة، بس الجو حلو بالليل، تعالي ننزل نتمشى شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: fekra 7elwa, bas el-gaww 7elw bel-leil, ta3aali nenzel netmashsha shwayya.
dialogue.english: Nice idea, but the weather is nice in the evening, let's go out for a little walk.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Okay, and after that I'll call my family.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.transliteration: w ana hashoof es7aabi bokra bel-leil.
dialogue.english: And I'll see my friends tomorrow evening.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: هنام بدري الليلة، أنا مش قادرة أفتح عيني.
dialogue.transliteration: hanaam badri el-leila, ana mesh 2aadra aftah 3eeni.
dialogue.english: I'll sleep early tonight, I can't keep my eyes open.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Good night.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: And you too.

pair.english: What will we eat for dinner?

lessons.culture: The reply to تصبح على خير is وإنت من أهل الخير, which does not translate word for word. Egyptian evenings start late: streets and cafés stay busy well after dinner, and a walk out with family or friends is a common way to end the day.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مساء الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but literary, not the everyday reply.

exercises.tip: مساء النور is the fixed reply to مساء الخير, just as صباح النور answers the morning greeting.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "تصبح على خير". Reply with the usual phrase.

too_formal.feedback: This spells it in the formal way and adds a word nobody says out loud.

exercises.tip: Saying تصبح على خير back is understood, but locals answer with وإنت من أهل الخير.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هنتعشى _____؟" English meaning: What will we eat for dinner?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, but Egyptians say إيه for what.

exercises.tip: إيه comes last in the question: هنتعشى إيه؟

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "تعبت _____ النهارده." English meaning: I got very tired today.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but far more formal than everyday Egyptian.

exercises.tip: أوي goes after the word it strengthens: تعبت أوي, حلو أوي.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "I came back home."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not what people say at home.

exercises.tip: رجعت البيت needs no preposition; البيت is the everyday word for home.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to shower."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, but not the spoken form.

exercises.tip: Egyptians take a shower: آخد دش, literally I take a shower.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll sleep early tonight."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not the spoken form.

exercises.tip: The future is ha + verb: هنام means I'll sleep; الليلة means tonight.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's go out for a little walk"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but sounds like a written invitation, not a friend's suggestion.

exercises.tip: تعالى means come here and is used to start a suggestion; a woman is told تعالي.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Do we want to watch a series?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far too formal for a living-room suggestion.

exercises.tip: تحب plus a verb is the everyday way to suggest something: shall we...?

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "أكلم / أهلي / عايز"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not the spoken sentence.

exercises.tip: عايز + verb is I want to...; أكلم means I talk to.

phrases.arabic: الْحَد، الاتْنين، التِّلات، الأرْبَع، الْخَميس، الْجُمْعَة، السَّبْت
phrases.transliteration: el-7ad, el-etneen, et-talaat, el-arba3, el-khamees, el-gom3a, es-sabt

phrases.arabic: الأسْبُوع الْجاي فيه اجْتِمَاع يَوْم التِّلات
phrases.transliteration: el-osboo3 el-gaay feeh egtimaa3 yoom et-talaat

phrases.arabic: نَاوي تَعْمِل إيه في الْويك إنْد؟
عِنْدي شُغِل كُلّ يَوْم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
phrases.transliteration: 3andi shoghl kol yoom gheer el-gom3a wes-sabt

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Today is Sunday, right?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، وبكرة الاتنين، يعني الأسبوع بدأ.
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, w bokra el-etneen, ya3ni el-osboo3 bada2.
dialogue.english: Yes, and tomorrow is Monday, so the week has started.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: When is the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: الأسبوع الجاي فيه اجتماع يوم التلات.
dialogue.transliteration: el-osboo3 el-gaay feeh egtimaa3 yoom et-talaat.
dialogue.english: Next week there's a meeting on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Okay, and on Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: On Wednesday I work until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.transliteration: w ana yoom el-khamees bashoof es7aabi.
dialogue.english: And on Thursday I see my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: والجمعة يوم صلاة وراحة، هصلي الجمعة وأرتاح.
dialogue.transliteration: wel-gom3a yoom salaa w raa7a, hasalli el-gom3a w artaa7.
dialogue.english: And Friday is the day of prayer and rest, I'll pray Jumu'a and relax.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: نَاوي تَعْمِل إيه في الْويك إنْد؟
dialogue.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: On Saturday we go to the market.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: The weekend comes quickly!

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، عندي شغل كل يوم غير الجمعة والسبت.
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, 3andi shoghl kol yoom gheer el-gom3a wes-sabt.
dialogue.english: Yes, I have work every day except Friday and Saturday.

pair.english: What do you do on Thursday?

pair.arabic: نَاوي تَعْمِل إيه في الْويك إنْد؟
pair.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

response.english: I'll go to the market on Saturday.

lessons.culture: The working week runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend for most offices. Friday is the Jumu'a prayer and family day. Sunday is said الحد in everyday speech (الأحد is the fuller form), and إمتى is the everyday word for when.

exercises.prompt: A colleague asks: "الاجتماع إمتى؟" Say it is tomorrow at ten.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but reads like a written notice, not a spoken reply.

exercises.tip: بكرة means tomorrow, and الساعة + number gives the time.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "ناوي تعمل إيه في الويك إند؟" Say you'll go to the market on Saturday.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not how a friend would say it.

exercises.tip: نزل is the everyday verb for going out to the market or the street.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "النهارده _____." English meaning: Today is Sunday.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but stiff; Egyptians say النهارده and just name the day.

exercises.tip: The day needs no verb or يوم: النهارده الحد. Many people also say الأحد in full.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الجمعة يوم _____ وراحة." English meaning: Friday is the day of prayer and rest.

too_formal.feedback: This is a general word for worship and is not the one used for the Friday prayer.

exercises.tip: يوم plus a noun is the everyday way to say the day of ...

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "Tomorrow is Monday."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not the spoken form.

exercises.tip: Egyptians say الاتنين for Monday and don't add a verb.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "On Thursday I see my friends."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not what friends say to each other.

exercises.tip: The b- prefix makes the verb habitual: بشوف means I see or I usually see.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "When is the meeting?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, but Egyptians say إمتى and put it last.

exercises.tip: إمتى is the everyday word for when, and it usually comes at the end.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The weekend comes quickly"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but written-style, not the spoken sentence.

exercises.tip: الويك إند is the everyday word; بييجي means it comes.

exercises.prompt: Which word is "Tuesday" in Egyptian speech?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but it is the written form, not what is said aloud.

exercises.tip: Egyptians drop the ث sound and say التلات, just as it is said for the number three.

exercises.prompt: Put these pieces in a natural order: "الجمعة والسبت / غير / كل يوم / شغل / عندي"
exercises.answer: عِنْدي شُغِل كُلّ يَوْم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
accepted: عِنْدي شُغِل كُلّ يَوْم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
كل يوم عندي شغل غير الجمعة والسبت
3andi shoghl kol yoom gheer el-gom3a wes-sabt

too_formal.item: لدي عمل كل يوم ما عدا الجمعة والسبت
too_formal.feedback: This is correct MSA, not the spoken sentence.

exercises.tip: غير means except or other than, and it is used before the days left out.

challenge.title: Plan Your Week in Egyptian
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short conversation about a day and the week ahead, at least 10 lines. It must include a morning greeting and its reply, a question about the time, a statement about being tired or sleepy, an evening greeting and its reply, the good-night exchange, a question about a day of the week or a meeting time, and a plan for the weekend. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 7.
required_elements: A morning greeting using صباح الخير and its reply صباح النور.
A statement about waking up or being sleepy, using صحيت بدري or لسه نعسان.
A question using الساعة كام؟ and a time answer.
A statement about being tired or having a lot of work, using تعبت or عندي شغل كتير.
An evening greeting using مساء الخير and its reply مساء النور.
The good-night exchange using تصبح على خير and وإنت من أهل الخير.
A question using إمتى؟ and its answer.
A statement naming at least two days of the week.
A plan for the weekend using الويك إند.
At least one invitation or suggestion, such as تحب تيجي؟ or تعالى ننزل.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير يا منى، عاملة إيه؟
dialogue.english: Good morning, Mona, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور، الحمد لله، بس لسه نعسانة شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7 en-noor, el-7amdu lillah, bas lessa na3saana shwayya.
dialogue.english: Good morning, praise God, but still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: الساعة سبعة، لازم أنزل على الشغل بسرعة.
dialogue.transliteration: es-saa3a sab3a, laazem anzel 3ala esh-shoghl bsor3a.
dialogue.english: It's seven, I have to leave for work quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Okay, when is the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: يوم التلات الساعة عشرة، وعندي شغل كتير دلوقتي.
dialogue.transliteration: yoom et-talaat es-saa3a 3ashra, w 3andi shoghl ketir dilwa2ti.
dialogue.english: Tuesday at ten, and I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: And you, on Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: يوم الأربع باشتغل لحد المسا، بس يوم الخميس هشوف صحابي.
dialogue.transliteration: yoom el-arba3 bashtaghal la7add el-masa, bas yoom el-khamees hashoof es7aabi.
dialogue.english: On Wednesday I work until the evening, but on Thursday I'll see my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مساء الخير يا منى، رجعت البيت.
dialogue.transliteration: masaa2 el-kheer ya Mona, rege3t el-beet.
dialogue.english: Good evening, Mona, I'm back home.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Good evening, I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: ناوية تعملي إيه في الويك إند؟ تعالي ننزل السوق يوم السبت.
dialogue.transliteration: nawya te3meli eh fel-weekend? ta3aali nenzel es-soo2 yoom es-sabt.
dialogue.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend? Come, let's go to the market on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Okay, the weekend comes quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: تصبحي على خير، هنام بدري الليلة.
dialogue.english: Good night, I'll sleep early tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: And you too.
